title: Ground fog is a fog term, never a translucent plane above the floor
note: A translucent horizontal plane above the floor cuts through every crate and reads as water; ground fog is a fog term or a floor-hugging texture.
intent: A translucent horizontal quad floating half a metre up intersects every crate and character at exactly one height, which the eye reads as a water line: the room looks flooded. Do ground fog with a height-based fog term in the material or a vertical-gradient shader, or with a texture lying on the floor at y near zero, or with a few soft sprites at varying heights and orientations. Never one big plane at a fixed height above the floor.

check.js: objects().filter(o => o.isMesh && o.material && (o.material.transparent || o.material.blending === 2) && o.geometry && o.geometry.type === 'PlaneGeometry' && Math.abs(Math.abs(o.rotation.x) - Math.PI / 2) < 0.01).every(o => { const b = bboxOf(o); return !b || b.min[1] <= 0.05; })
check.note: No translucent or additive horizontal plane sits above the floor: a haze plane at 0.3-0.8 m cuts through every crate and reads as 'filled with water'. Ground fog is a vertical-gradient fog term or a floor-hugging texture at y<=0.05.

port: The atmosphere facet owns the fog term; nothing else adds a horizontal transparent plane above y = 0.05.
